q: What changes between steel and cement CBAM figures for exporters in Vietnam's Ha Tinh and Nghi Son corridor?
title: Vietnam steel vs cement CBAM figures
short: Steel is charged on direct emissions only, so coal and coke in the blast furnace set the figure and electricity is left out. Cement is charged on direct and indirect emissions, so calcination, kiln fuel and electricity all count. The two need different monitoring plans.
audience: Steel and cement producers in the Ha Tinh and Nghi Son corridor in Vietnam and their EU buyers

ul: Direct emissions only, under Annex II of the CBAM Regulation.
Main sources: coal and coke in the blast furnace, sinter and pellet plants, reheating furnaces.
Precursors: sinter or pellets, pig iron, and any bought DRI or ferro-alloys.
Main sources: calcination of limestone, kiln fuel, and electricity for mills and fans.
Precursor: clinker, if a grinding unit buys it.

p: A group with both a steel plant and a cement plant can use one accredited verifier, but each installation needs its own monitoring and its own embedded emissions per CN code. Blast furnace slag sent to cement grinding carries no embedded emissions into the cement under CBAM, because slag is not a CBAM good.
